newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MVP GONZALEZ'S THUMB INJURY MORE SERIOUS THAN THOUGHT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MVP GONZALEZ'S THUMB INJURY MORE SERIOUS THAN THOUGHT.

text.p: The thumb injury suffered last month by American League Most Valuable Player Juan Gonzalez of the Texas Rangers is more serious than team officials initially believed, the club said Thursday.
An MRI performed on Thursday indicated that damage to a ligament in the outfielder's left thumb warrants further evaluation, the team said.
The Rangers originally said Gonzalez would be ready for the start of spring training. Team officials now say they do not know how long the 27-year-old slugger will be sidelined.
Gonzalez suffered the injury last week while diving for a ball in the Puerto Rican winter league championship series.
In the major leagues last season, Gonzalez batted .314 with 47 homers and 144 RBI, leading the Rangers to their first American League Western Division title.
Gonzalez hit a record-tying five homers and drove in nine runs in the AL Divisional Playoffs, but the Rangers lost to the eventual World Series champion New York Yankees in four games.
Pitchers and catchers will report to the Rangers' spring training camp in Port Charlotte, Florida, on February 13. Position players are scheduled to report February 19.
